newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel weighs security if it cedes parts of Golan.
newsitem.headline: Israel weighs security if it cedes parts of Golan.

text.p: Israel's defence minister has ordered the army to examine the country's security needs should Israel return parts of the Golan Heights to Syria in a peace deal, a newspaper and security sources said on Wednesday.

They said Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai ordered the review despite Likud Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's refusal to cede any of the strategic plateau captured from Syria in the 1967 Middle East War.
Israel's Maariv newspaper said Mordechai had asked the defence establishment for answers to the question: "How is it possible to protect northern Israel without parts of the Golan Heights?"
A security source, confirming the report, said: "There are all kinds of scenarios and they're checking them...These are possible solutions to the Israeli-Syrian track."

Netanyahu, elected eight months ago, told the newspaper Haaretz he would raise "various ideas" for breaking the deadlock with Syria when he meets U.S. President Bill Clinton at the White House next month. He did not specify the ideas.

Washington is trying to get Israel and Syria to revive peace talks launched in 1991 but suspended by Israel's previous government 10 months ago following four Islamist suicide bombings which killed 59 people in Israel.

Mordechai has examined the work done by the defence establishment for the previous Labour-led government, ousted by Netanyahu, which was ready to return at least part of the Golan for peace with Syria, Mordechai's spokesman Avi Benayahu said.
He emphasised that Mordechai had not ordered the army to prepare any plans for a withdrawal.

Israel's pullback from most of the West Bank town of Hebron this month has revived interest in talks with Syria. Netanyahu's avowed refusal to swap any of the Golan for peace has raised Syrian suspicions he is not committed to peace.
Damascus demands the return of all of the heights.
On Tuesday night Syrian Vice-President Abdel-Halim Khaddam brushed aside Israeli suggestions their bilateral Middle East peace talks were about to resume.

"There is no movement until now regarding resumption of talks on the Syrian and Lebanese tracks," he said after talks with United Arab Emirates President Sheikh Zaid bin Sultan al-Nahayan in Abu Dhabi.
In the interview with Haaretz, Netanyahu said he foresaw economic talks with Syria whenever peace moves resumed and he had asked Finance Minister Dan Meridor to work on the issue.

"Syria will have much to gain on the economic side because the Syrian economy is not dashing forward. There are certain things that only with an open approach -- like joint projects -- will Syria be able to make progress," he said.
